releases.title: Mentor Collective Launches Flash Mentoring to Close the Career Readiness Gap in Higher Education
releases.body:
New flexible mentoring model gives every student access to alumni expertise, complementing Mentor Collective's Structured Mentoring programs

BOSTON, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mentor Collective, higher education's preferred edtech platform for student mentorship, announced the launch of Flash Mentoring, a new, purposeful model built around focused, single-session conversations between students and alumni. Flash Mentoring joins Mentor Collective's existing Structured Mentoring model to support the full arc of the student journey, from belonging to employability, on one platform.

Higher education institutions are under unprecedented pressure to demonstrate career readiness, workforce outcomes, and degree ROI. Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Mentor Collective meets students right where they are. With Flash Mentoring, every student has a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

"Every student's path looks different, and their support should too," said Patrick Garayta, Chief Executive Officer of Mentor Collective. "Some students want an ongoing relationship with a peer mentor. Others need the right person with the right experience for one purposeful conversation. Flash Mentoring and Structured Mentoring are built for exactly that reason, and together, they mean no students' needs will fall through the cracks."

Flash Mentoring is also designed with alumni in mind. Traditional engagement strategies, from reunions to newsletters to committee service, reach only a small fraction of a given alumni base. Flash offers a flexible, time-boxed way for alumni to give back in a single conversation, activating graduates who would never respond to a longer commitment. At the same time, advancement and alumni relations teams gain a new, trackable form of engagement to bring to leadership.

"Career offices and advancement teams keep telling us the same thing: their networks are bigger than their engagement numbers show," said Jennifer Kious, Director of Marketing at Mentor Collective. "Flash Mentoring is specifically built to reach the alumni who are typically disengaged. Every conversation becomes data our partners can use to tell a clearer story about alumni engagement and student outcomes."

Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build that access: a focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, without the long-term commitment of a traditional mentoring program. For alumni, it offers a meaningful, flexible way to give back on their own schedule. For institutions, every conversation becomes a logged, reportable data point that strengthens the case for continued investment in student success.

Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: a single, focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

Flash Mentoring is available now to all higher education institutions, on its own or alongside Structured Mentoring, through the same co-branded experience and reporting dashboard partners already use to track student outcomes.

Mentor Collective expects Flash Mentoring to help partner institutions nationwide expand access to career readiness support, close equity gaps in social capital, and give alumni a meaningful, low-lift way to stay connected to their alma mater.

To learn more about Flash Mentoring, visit mentorcollective.org.

About Mentor Collective

Mentor Collective is an education technology provider that drives student enrollment, retention, and career readiness through research-backed, scalable mentorship solutions. The company's mission is to ensure every learner realizes their full potential through connections, confidence, and support—not by chance, but by design. Mentor Collective enables institutions to embed personalized mentorship into the fabric of the learner experience, strengthening belonging, closing social capital gaps, and accelerating career readiness. Backed by over a decade of results, Mentor Collective supports more than one million participants across 200+ partnerships.

releases.title: The Inner Circle acknowledges Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez as a Pinnacle Professional of The Year
releases.body:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M., Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Prominently featured in The Inner Circle, Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez is acknowledged as a Pinnacle Professional of The Year for his contributions to Mathematics Education and Student Success.

Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez has built a distinguished career in higher education, dedicating nearly four decades to teaching and advancing mathematics education. As a retired faculty member of the University of New Mexico, he is recognized for his commitment to student success and his ability to make complex mathematical concepts accessible to learners at all levels.

Dr. Martinez specialized in mathematics education, graduate statistics, calculus, and algebra, with a particular focus on reducing math anxiety. His teaching approach emphasized patience and step by step instruction, helping students build confidence and develop a deeper understanding of mathematical principles. His methods have inspired many students to pursue further studies and careers in mathematics.

He earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Education and Mathematics, with concentrations in mathematics education and educational psychology, from the University of New Mexico in 1980. His academic background provided a strong foundation for his work in both teaching and research design.

Throughout his career, Dr. Martinez taught at the University of New Mexico until his retirement in 2012 and also held earlier teaching roles at the University of Albuquerque. Over the years, he became widely respected for his engaging teaching style and dedication to supporting student achievement.

In addition to his work in the classroom, Dr. Martinez is an accomplished author, having written eight books and more than 200 published articles. His book Math Without Fear, along with other works including those coauthored with his late wife Nancy, reflects his mission to make mathematics more approachable and less intimidating for students.

Dr. Martinez credits his wife, Nancy, as a key influence in refining his teaching philosophy and instructional methods. Her support and insight played an important role in shaping his approach to education.

Looking ahead, Dr. Martinez is exploring opportunities to expand his educational outreach, particularly within Orthodox Jewish communities. Guided by a philosophy that anyone can learn mathematics with the right support and instruction, he remains committed to sharing his knowledge and helping others overcome challenges in learning.

releases.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ALPFA proudly announced the recipients of its 2026 Student Scholarship Program during the 2026 ALPFA Convention, awarding $1.4 million to 334 students in recognition of their academic excellence, leadership, and commitment to making a lasting impact in their communities across North America. This year's scholarship recipients reflect the talent, resilience and ambition shaping the future of business, technology, healthcare, finance, public service and entrepreneurship. With awards ranging from $2,500 to $10,000, the program represents ALPFA's continued investment in expanding access to higher education and professional opportunity.

Join us in expanding pathways to education, opportunity and career growth for the next generation of leaders. Support ALPFA's continued investment in students and communities.

Impact in Action

The ALPFA 2026 Student Scholarship Program awarded $1.4 million to 334 students, representing 122 colleges and universities across 31 states. The recipients included 240 first-generation college students and 203 students across 52 Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), highlighting the program's reach across institutions serving our communities nationwide.

A Commitment to Opportunity

"At ALPFA, we want every student to see a future where their culture and their career pull in the same direction where who they are becomes a source of strength in who they are becoming. These scholarships help create that future by expanding access to education, opportunity, relationships and experiences that can change the trajectory of a life. We are proudly rooted in Latino culture and open to all, building a community where people can learn from one another, lead authentically and use their success to create opportunity for the people who follow. When we invest in these students, we are investing in the leaders who will help build a better future for all of us." said Damian Rivera, President and CEO of ALPFA

The ALPFA Student Scholarship Program is designed to remove financial barriers to higher education while connecting students to a national network of mentors, corporate partners, and career development opportunities. Reflecting ALPFA's commitment to creating pathways to opportunity, the scholarship program welcomes students across all majors and backgrounds who meet application, academic and enrollment criteria. Beyond academic achievement, recipients are recognized for their leadership, service, resilience, and commitment to advancing their community.

"At ALPFA, investing in our students' education is a commitment to the dreams of our community," said Maria V. Fernandez, Student Programs Manager. "We see education as an accelerator, one that can transform the trajectory of a student's life and create an impact that reaches far beyond any single award. When we invest in them, we are also investing in the people they will mentor, the doors they will open, and the generations that will follow. That is how a scholarship becomes more than financial support. It becomes a lasting legacy of opportunity."

With more than 1,400 applications, the 2026 scholarship recipients represent a diverse group of emerging leaders bringing their own experiences, ambitions and perspectives to the next chapter of their academic and professional journeys. They are pursuing degrees across a wide range of disciplines, including business, engineering, healthcare, technology, and more, reflecting the strength and diversity of multicultural talent across undergraduate, graduate, and community college programs.

Meet the Scholars

Hear directly from some of our scholarship recipients and learn about their experiences here. 

Several recipients shared what receiving an ALPFA scholarship means to them:

"You have given me more than a scholarship—you have given me the confidence to push forward, knowing that I am not just building a career for myself, but a pathway for those who will follow in my footsteps." – Daniela Correa, Hult International Business School



"Beyond the financial support, this recognition serves as a reminder that hard work, perseverance, and community involvement matter. Through ALPFA, I have developed valuable leadership skills, built meaningful relationships, and gained access to opportunities that have shaped my career path. This scholarship motivates me to continue striving for excellence, give back to my community, and create opportunities for others who share similar aspirations." – Lorelys Alvarez, Lehman College CUNY

Creating Pathways for What's Next

The 2026 Student Scholarship Program was made possible through the generous support of our partners, whose commitment helped ALPFA award $1.4 million to 334 students. Their investment extends beyond financial support, helping scholars pursue their ambitions, build on their strengths and translate their potential into meaningful career impact.

This year, 8 scholarship recipients were also selected for fellowship opportunities, extending that investment through continued professional development, mentorship and career experiences. Together, these opportunities help prepare the next generation of professionals to contribute, lead and shape the future of the workforce.

Scholarships are one of the many ways ALPFA invests in the next generation of leaders. Through 270+ student chapters and 50+ professional chapters, ALPFA provides year-round access to career resources, mentorship, bootcamps, leadership development and a nationwide professional network. At the 2026 ALPFA Convention, 5,800+ attendees—including 3,200+ professionals, 2,600+ students, 370+ executives and 250+ speakers—came together, creating opportunities for students to connect with leading employers, expand their networks, build career-ready skills and take the next step in their professional journeys.

Learn more about our scholarship eligibility requirements and application criteria and fellowship opportunities designed to support students' continued professional development and career growth.

Join us in building pathways to opportunity and investing in the leaders of tomorrow. 

About ALPFA

Founded in 1972, ALPFA is the nation's leading professional association dedicated to empowering and developing leaders. With a nationwide network of professional and student chapters, ALPFA provides leadership development, career opportunities, mentorship, and community to professionals and students across every stage of their careers. Through strategic partnerships with leading organizations, ALPFA continues to create pathways for the next generation of leaders while advancing representation across every industry.

releases.body:
Pioneering D.C. nonprofit welcomes its newest university partner, unlocking financial aid and wraparound services for college-ready students in the District

WASHINGTON, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The DC College Access Program (DC CAP), a nonprofit dedicated to eliminating the higher education achievement gap for Washington, D.C. students, announced American University as its newest university partner today. The collaboration will expand access to higher education pathways that change lives and strengthen communities in the nation's capital.

"Together with DC CAP, we're taking a critical next step toward closing the college opportunity gap for D.C. students. Washington, D.C. isn't just where American University is located, it's our home, and we have a responsibility to ensure that talented students across the District can see a path to an AU education," said Jeremy Lowe, interim vice president of Undergraduate Enrollment Management at American University. "Our partnership with DC CAP strengthens that commitment by helping more D.C. students obtain access, afford, and ultimately thrive in college."

American University joins DC CAP's broader network of University Partners, which provide eligible D.C. students with the support and structure they need to thrive in college, from application to degree completion. Students who participate in the University Partnerships program are more likely to persist through college than their peers: 85% of freshmen continue on to their sophomore year, and 57-100% graduate from college within five years, 3-5 times the national average, reducing the likelihood of accruing unnecessary educational debt and opening the door to greater economic and career opportunities.

As a DC CAP University Partner, American University certifies its commitment to ensuring every college-ready D.C. student has the financial resources, coaching, and community they need to succeed. American University will collaborate closely with DC CAP to maximize financial aid availability, stacking DC CAP scholarships, Pell Grants, D.C. Tuition Assistance Grants (DCTAG), and institutional aid with the goal of helping D.C. students finish college with little to no debt. The partnership will also provide tailored academic and socio-emotional support to D.C. students, from enrollment to graduation.

"For so many of our scholars, staying close to the community they grew up in matters, and having one of the nation's top universities just a short Metro ride away means they don't have to choose between a great education and home," said Eric Waldo, executive director of DC CAP. "We couldn't be more thrilled to be joining forces with American University. This partnership will help turn proximity into opportunity, and ensure that more students in the District can access the support they need to learn and thrive."

Students who are interested in participating in DC CAP programs can confirm their eligibility by taking a short online survey, which opens on October 15, and then applying in January 2027. For more information, please visit www.dccap.org/programs/university-partners.

About the DC College Access Program

The DC College Access Program (DC CAP Scholars) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to eliminating the higher education achievement gap for D.C. students by helping them access and attain meaningful college degrees with little to no debt. DC CAP Scholars believes that a student's personal circumstances should never determine their ability to succeed. By leveraging dollars, connecting students to better match universities, and providing wraparound support, DC CAP Scholars works to ensure students graduate ready to compete in today's economy.

About American University

American University leverages the power and purpose of scholarship, learning, and community to impact our changing world. AU's faculty, students, staff, and alumni shape the future from artificial intelligence to civic life and the sciences. Building on our 133-year history of education and research, AU is committed to addressing the world's pressing issues.

releases.body:
Fellowships designed to support first-generation and Pell-eligible students now open for the 2027 academic year.

PORTLAND, Maine, Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Council on International Educational Exchange (CIEE) is the leader in providing opportunities for first-generation and Pell-eligible students to study abroad, awarding over $13 million each year in grants and scholarships to study and intern abroad.

"We are committed to increasing access to all college students from all backgrounds, especially for first generation and underserved populations, to ensure that all students can experience and benefit from the powerful impact of studying abroad," said James P. Pellow, Ed.D., President and CEO, CIEE.

Douglass O'Connell Global Internship Program

Established in 2015, the Douglass–O'Connell Global Internship Program in Ireland prepares high-achieving, Pell-eligible students for future career success through the power of international education and a global internship. Sponsored by Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs, the African American Irish Diaspora Network (AAIDN), The John and Lillian Miles Lewis Foundation, and CIEE, the program celebrates the inspiration that Frederick Douglass experienced during his visit to Ireland over 175 years ago when he met the elder statesman and his personal hero, Daniel O'Connell. O'Connell and Douglass spent their lives advocating for equality and opportunity in Ireland, the United States, and around the world.

Thirteen students are selected each year for an 8-week global internship in Dublin, including full program funding, airfare, and a living stipend. Following in the footsteps of Frederick Douglass and Daniel O'Connell, students will experience Ireland through lectures and excursions, learning important lessons on leadership and social reform while gaining important skills that will enhance their future careers.

Applications for the Douglass O'Connell Global Internship Program are open and close on January 8, 2027.

Scan Design Foundation Environmental Sustainability Internship

Established in 2025, the Scan Design Foundation Environmental Sustainability Internship in Copenhagen, Denmark focuses on advancing Danish American relations by supporting cultural exchange focused on environmental sustainability. Twelve students will have the opportunity to study and intern with a company in Copenhagen focused on environmentally sustainable business practices for 8 weeks. Students also will explore Danish sustainability culture and participate in networking and professional development activities. Open to Pell-eligible students, the fellowship equips participants with practical skills to enhance their career readiness and tackle future environmental challenges.

The Scan Design Foundation honors the legacy of Danish immigrants, Inger & Jens Bruun, to advance Danish-American relations by supporting cultural exchanges focused on environmental sustainability.

Applications for the Scan Design Foundation Environmental Sustainability Internship are open and close on November 20, 2026.

"Few experiences rival the impact of a global internship for preparing students for life after graduation," explained Patrick Moran, Senior Vice President for College Study Abroad, CIEE. "Students selected for these programs will gain important problem solving, intercultural communication, and self-leadership skills most valued by employers in today's globally interconnected workplace."

Knowledge Without Borders: Democracy and Memory Fellowship

Established in 2026 by a generous gift from Karen Collias, The Knowledge Without Borders: Democracy and Memory Fellowship is designed for first-generation, Pell-eligible students who are passionate about history, political science, civic leadership, social justice, and global affairs. Through this fellowship, four exceptional students receive $10,000 each toward a CIEE Quarter In or CIEE Open Campus study abroad program in Berlin, Germany.

Fellows explore Berlin's storied history, including how the city has been shared by reflection, memorialization, and democratic responsibility. The fellowship includes courses on German history and Berlin's cultural and political landscape while students explore one of the world's most important living classrooms.

Applications are open for the Spring 2027 Knowledge Without Borders: Democracy and Memory Fellowship and close on November 1, 2026.

About CIEE

Since 1947, CIEE has built bridges between different people, countries, and cultures through study abroad and international exchange programs that advance peace in our world. We change lives; our alumni change the world. Learn more at ciee.org.

The scholarship serves as a platform to recognize students who view science not merely as a subject of study, but as a collaborative endeavor with far-reaching societal implications. By providing financial assistance and public recognition, the Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship aims to alleviate some of the burdens associated with higher education, allowing recipients to focus more intently on their research and academic goals.

Candidates must pursue a degree in a science-related field and maintain a strong academic record, evidenced by official transcripts. Additionally, applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Dr. Kerry Evans brings over two decades of experience in high-pressure medical environments to this philanthropic effort. As a dedicated emergency room physician, he understands the importance of precision, dedication, and continuous learning.

Applicants must submit a 1,000-word essay addressing the specified prompt, official transcripts from their current institution, and letters of recommendation from professors or qualified professionals who can attest to their academic potential. All materials must be sent to apply@drkerryevansscholarship.com by the deadline of May 15, 2027.

The winner of this one-time award will be announced on June 15, 2027. This timeline allows the selection committee ample time to review submissions thoroughly and ensure that the recipient truly embodies the spirit of scientific curiosity and academic diligence.

For those interested in learning more about the requirements or the vision behind the initiative, detailed information is available at https://drkerryevansscholarship.com/.

The Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship for Sciences was established by Dr. Kerry Evans, a seasoned emergency room physician with a deep commitment to education and healthcare advancement. Founded to support undergraduate students pursuing science-related degrees, the organization aims to reduce financial barriers and encourage academic excellence. releases.title: FaverGray Named a 2026 Best Place to Work by Jacksonville Business Journal
releases.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FaverGray, a general contractor specializing in multifamily and student housing construction, has been named one of the Jacksonville Business Journal's 2026 Best Places to Work, recognizing the company among Northeast Florida employers known for creating strong workplace cultures.

The annual Best Places to Work program recognizes companies throughout the First Coast based on feedback from their employees, with confidential surveys evaluating areas including team dynamics, trust in leadership, communication and overall workplace experience.

For FaverGray, the recognition comes at an exciting time of growth. As the company continues to grow, so does its team, creating new opportunities for employees to advance their careers, take on greater responsibilities and contribute to FaverGray's future.

"Our people have always been the foundation of FaverGray," said James A. Gray, CEO of FaverGray. "As we've grown, we've worked hard to maintain a culture where people enjoy coming to work, feel valued as part of the team and have opportunities to grow with the company. Being recognized as a Best Place to Work is especially meaningful because it comes from the feedback of our own employees."

That culture extends beyond the work itself. FaverGray makes it a priority to bring its team together throughout the year, whether it's a monthly food truck at the Jacksonville Beach office, holiday celebrations, team outings or company events. Most recently, employees and their families spent an afternoon together at Beach Bowl for FaverGray's Family Day, and the team is already looking forward to its annual Chili Cook-Off this fall.

STAMFORD, Conn., Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How much life insurance does a family really need in Stamford, Connecticut? In a HelloNation article, Burak Kaya of The Wright Agency shares insights to help families calculate the right coverage amount and avoid financial shortfalls during life's most difficult moments.

The HelloNation article explains that life insurance provides critical protection by replacing lost income, covering outstanding debts, and supporting long-term goals such as college tuition and retirement savings. Determining the right policy amount depends on factors like household income, number of dependents, debts, and future expenses. A customized approach ensures that family life insurance offers meaningful protection without unnecessary cost.

A common guideline is to calculate enough coverage to replace several years of household income. The article notes that if a primary earner passes away unexpectedly, life insurance can help maintain the family's standard of living during the adjustment period. For a two-parent household with young children, the amount of coverage often needs to cover essentials like the mortgage, childcare, utilities, and food for multiple years.

Outstanding debts also play a major role in determining coverage. The article explains that families should consider mortgages, car loans, credit card balances, and personal loans when calculating how much life insurance they need. Including these obligations can help reduce the financial burden on surviving family members.

Future expenses must also be considered in the coverage calculation. The article points to college tuition, healthcare, and retirement planning as common long-term goals. In Stamford, CT, where education costs and local activity fees may exceed national averages, families may also need to include private school tuition, extracurricular programs, and seasonal childcare when determining their coverage amount.

The HelloNation article describes how the type of life insurance policy also impacts both coverage and cost. Term life insurance offers protection for a set period, often aligned with mortgage terms or child dependency years. Whole life insurance provides lifelong coverage and includes a cash value component, but comes with higher premiums. Universal life insurance allows flexibility and includes an investment element. Choosing the right type of policy depends on each family's financial goals, budget, and long-term planning needs.

Household assets, savings, and emergency funds also influence how much life insurance is appropriate. The article explains that families with significant savings may not require as much coverage, while households with fewer resources may need a larger policy to ensure stability. Reviewing assets and liabilities together helps create a complete picture of what the policy must cover.

The article emphasizes that different households require different levels of protection. Single-parent families, blended families, and multigenerational households may need to account for responsibilities such as caring for a child with special needs, providing long-term care, or supporting a spouse. Reviewing these obligations helps families choose coverage that reflects their actual financial needs.

The HelloNation article encourages policy reviews every few years or whenever there are major life changes, such as a new child, home purchase, or income change. Regular updates help keep coverage aligned with evolving goals and ensure that beneficiaries remain accurate.

By evaluating income replacement, outstanding debts, future expenses, and available savings, families in Stamford, CT, can build a solid life insurance strategy. The article notes that careful planning results in coverage that meets needs without high cost.

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Princeton Review®, a provider of education services and college admission resources since 1981, today released the 35th edition of its annual guide to getting funding to pay for college.

Paying for College: Everything You Need to Maximize Financial Aid and Afford College (2027 Edition, Penguin Random House, September 22, 2026, $25.99) is authored by Kalman A. Chany, a nationally recognized expert on college funding, with Geoff Martz. Chany is founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent college financial aid advisory firm based in New York City.

When Paying for College debuted in 1992, it was a one-of-a-kind resource in the category of personal finance guides. It provided detailed line-by-line guidance on strategically completing the two most important financial aid application forms for the upcoming aid application year, and it was the only book to do so.

Paying for College remains the only resource offering such targeted guidance for submitting those two crucial forms. They are the U.S. Department of Education's FAFSA® (Free Application for Federal Student Aid), which all financial aid applicants must submit, and the College Board's CSS Profile®, an application that hundreds of selective colleges require (and which has as many as 200 questions).

"You might think that families who receive the most financial aid would be the families with the most need," Chany says in the introduction of the book. "In fact, this is not necessarily true. The people who receive the most aid are the people who best understand the aid process." 

Chany well understands the process. Since 1981, he has annually analyzed the major aid application forms as well as the formulas by which federal and institutional financial aid administrators assess an applicant's need for aid based on answers on the forms. He guides his clients (and readers of this book) on how to maximize their eligibility for financial aid much in the same way an accountant advises clients on submitting their IRS returns to their best advantage. (All the strategies Chany recommends follow the law to the letter.)

In Paying for College, Chany also covers other subjects important to aid applicants and parents, including how to:

  • explore long- and short-term strategies for reducing college costs
  • research colleges with financial aid in mind
  • compare financial aid offers and, if necessary, appeal for more aid
  • obtain education loans, understand payment plans, and manage loan debt

A Special Topics chapter in the book gives particular advice on aid applications for parents who are single, separated, divorced or in blended families as well as advice for students who are independent, international or older than the traditional applicant.

The 2027 edition of Paying for College also reports on tectonic changes that have impacted the college funding landscape as a result of various provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) signed into law in July 2025. Chany discusses what parents and students need to know about these changes. Icons in the margins flag topics that were pending as the book went to press that readers are advised to check.

Some provisions of the OBBBA that impact federal student aid are still unresolved. "Unfortunately," Chany notes, "some guidance involving federal education loans issued by the U.S. Department of Education is being misinterpreted—even by college aid professionals."

Over the years, Paying for College has been praised by reviewers and finance professionals alike. Forbes contributor John Wasik noted it "can save thousands in college bills." Washington Post syndicated columnist Michelle Singletary chose it for her Color of Money book club. Newsday Family Finance columnist Lynn Brenner recommended it as "a first-rate guide through the financial aid maze."

Said Rob Franek, Editor-in-Chief of The Princeton Review, "Our company has a deep appreciation for the concerns of students and parents about paying for college. Among nearly 10,000 college applicants and parents of applicants who completed our 2026 College Hopes & Worries Survey in February, 93% reported they would need financial aid to pay for college, and 81% of that cohort characterized their level of need as "very" or "extremely" necessary. We hope the advice in this new edition of Paying for College will help parents and students apply strategies to get all the financial aid they are entitled to and enable them to pay less for college."

Paying for College is one of more than 150 books developed by The Princeton Review and published by Penguin Random House in a line that includes The Best 392 Colleges  and guides to the SAT®, ACT®, and AP® exams. The Princeton Review is also known for its annual college rankings in dozens of categories including its popular "Great Financial Aid" college ranking list and its "Best Value Colleges" lists.

Kalman A. Chany is the founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent New York City-based financial aid advisory firm. For more than four decades, his firm has helped thousands of families maximize their financial aid eligibility and save tens of thousands of dollars off the cost of their children's college education. Kal has been sourced in The Wall Street Journal, on CNBC, and in Money magazine, and he has appeared on CBS Evening News, NBC Nightly News, and other broadcast media.

Together, the organizations will expand access to flexible, high-quality care by integrating Lavender's medication management services into the BetterMynd therapeutic ecosystem.

With one in three students reporting symptoms of moderate anxiety or depression (Healthy Minds, 2025), the demand for accessible care is at an all-time high. This partnership reflects a shared belief that students are best served by adaptable care models built around the individual. By combining their expertise, BetterMynd and Lavender can better respond to the full spectrum of mental health needs seen across the student population.

For educational institutions navigating growing demand and increasing complexity in student mental health, the partnership offers a high-quality, scalable solution that is easy to implement.

"Our mission is to make getting help easier for every college student, and we believe every student deserves an exceptional experience," said Cody Semrau, Founder and CEO of BetterMynd. "We're excited to partner with Lavender, an organization that shares our mission-driven focus and also puts the students first in all that they do. This ensures students have the most comprehensive resources available while providing institutions with a trusted, scalable model."

Accessing psychiatric care can often mean navigating long wait times, referrals between multiple providers, and limited prescribing options; barriers that can be especially challenging for student populations. Lavender removes this friction by providing integrated psychiatric services within BetterMynd's established care pathway, from assessment and prescribing to ongoing medication management, including ADHD treatment and controlled substances when clinically appropriate. A network of 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across more than 40 states, supported by customized referral pathways and dedicated administrative support, helps make that access seamless and scalable for BetterMynd's university partners.

releases.body:
Students begin new academic journeys in London, combining project-based learning, industry engagement and the opportunity to earn bachelor's and master's degrees in four years

LONDON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASU London has officially opened its academic year, welcoming students to a new international higher education experience built around project-based learning, real-world challenges and global opportunities.

"We have designed ASU London to provide students with a compelling new way they can both gain an international experience and prepare for their careers, in the U.K. and the U.S.," Arizona State University President Michael Crow said. "We're in the business of changing people's lives and futures. We will continue to expand our efforts and our impact to engage with learners all over the world."

ASU London — an independent U.K. degree-awarding higher education provider — will offer three-year bachelor's degrees in areas including business, computer science, engineering and design. Its programs are built around project-based learning and real-world experience, with students working on challenges shaped by industry and community needs, leading to opportunities for Arizona State University master's degrees.

"I don't think this has happened before, and that is what is so extraordinary," said Sir Malcolm Grant, grant chair of ASU London's board of trustee directors, a senior advisor to Crow and part of London's university system since 1972. "We can take students internationally, give them three years' education here in London, and then they may go onto a master's program (at ASU).

"Being able to offer students this extraordinary opportunity...I am totally committed to this."

The institution's approach places particular emphasis on future-focused skills, including artificial intelligence, technology and sustainable innovation. Students from different disciplines can work together on complex problems that require practical solutions and collaboration.

Those who pursue master's degrees at Arizona State University will gain exposure to one of the fastest-growing U.S. research universities, known for innovation, sustainability, the largest engineering school and its location within a region rapidly expanding in microelectronics and the knowledge economy.

"ASU is an exceptional partner in elevating Phoenix on the global stage, and I know ASU London will help our city and region take another important step forward," said Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego. "I look forward to continuing to work with Michael Crow and ASU to connect the world with the dynamic opportunities Phoenix and Arizona offer for innovation, investment and collaboration."

Tackling global challenges

ASU London is designed to prepare students for a changing world of work and the challenges facing communities around the world.

"The world's biggest challenges require collaboration across disciplines and borders," said ASU London Managing Director Michael Goodwin. "ASU London gives students the opportunity to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to contribute to those challenges while building careers in a changing global economy."

The opening of the academic year also begins a new phase in ASU London's relationship with the U.K. The institution is developing relationships with local communities, universities, employers, alumni and other organizations as it contributes to London's educational and innovation ecosystem.

Learn with industry

ASU London's hands-on approach reflects one of its central principles: to learn by doing. Students are encouraged to build, test and experience ideas through practical projects. They can work on issues including sustainability, artificial intelligence and smart cities while developing technical, professional and collaborative skills.

James Woods, who is studying business management after graduating from high school in Phoenix this May, said everything about ASU London — from its learning approach to its global focus — convinced him to cross the pond to begin his college education.

"I feel as I come to London, it's going to open up more opportunities for me to be a leader," Woods said. "You're surrounded by leaders. And what I particularly like is that they're not just handing you a paper to work on. You're actually working on a project. You're given a purpose."

Industry engagement is a core part of the ASU London learning experience. Students work on projects shaped by employers and build professional skills from day one. Through project-based learning, real-world challenges and industry engagement, students develop portfolios of work that demonstrate what they can do as well as what they know.

The institution's location in the heart of the city, at the Clerkenwell campus of City St. George's, University of London, also places students within a diverse environment of businesses, creative organizations, technology companies and cultural institutions.

"Effectively, we're giving them this very small, friendly and supportive community as part of ASU London," Goodwin said. "But they have access to a much wider, bigger university experience should they choose to take it up."

Connecting continents

ASU London also provides qualified graduates with opportunities to select one-year master's degrees at Arizona State University in the U.S., subject to program requirements and applicable U.S. immigration and visa requirements.

These include master's degrees in areas such as computer science, cybersecurity, electrical engineering, business analytics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing, artificial intelligence in business, economics, information systems management, supply chain management and user experience.

Beyond these one-year programs, qualified graduates from ASU London bachelor's degree programs will have additional pathways to the wider portfolio of Arizona State University graduate degrees.

This gives students the opportunity to begin with a U.K. bachelor's degree in London and continue their academic journey in the United States.

"What we're doing with ASU London is we're launching an experiment in academic innovation," Crow said. "We're launching an initiative where we can partner with more people in the U.K., an English-speaking country that's deeply connected with people all over the world.

"We're also trying to build in more agility for ourselves. You can't come to the United States? Well, maybe you can go to England."

For the 320 students beginning their studies this September, the new academic year represents the start of their own journey.

Among them are Gustavo Alves, a first-year student from Brazil who will major in business management. For him, the decision to enroll at ASU London was easy. It has everything he could want, both personally and professionally.

"The teenager life and the university life are great," said Alves. "And the professional side, with the job market, with the connections you can make with companies in London, I think it's a great city to be in."

Although ASU London is in its infancy, Crow already is thinking about the future. He said ASU London could have as many as 4,000 students and be a global model for other universities.

"We hope that it's a pilot for a global model because we're working with Cintana Education to not only help start universities around the world but to help enhance universities around the world," Crow said. "The education sector has under-innovated for the challenges that are ahead, and are very much focused on status and selectivity as their method of competition.

"So welcome, in a sense, to an innovative project."

releases.title: Disasterville Returns: Army National Guard Brings Mixed-Reality Disaster Response Missions Back to Schools
releases.body:
At a Glance

  • This fall, the U.S. Army National Guard's mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, is returning to high schools nationwide to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies. 
  • Disasterville guides students through high-tech, virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes in the same way as the Guard.
  • The Disasterville tour continues to introduce students to the possibilities available in the Army National Guard—a unique component within the U.S. Army where Soldiers have the flexibility to serve their country part-time while also pursuing a civilian career or higher education. 

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This fall, the Army National Guard's immersive mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, will begin its second nationwide tour of high schools, giving students a first-hand look at how to prepare for and respond to natural disasters—without leaving their schools. Disasterville is activating in high school gyms where it will take students through virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes, just like Soldiers responding to similar emergencies in communities across the country. This follows Disasterville's successful inaugural tour in spring 2026, which reached more than 2,000 students.

"Natural disasters are not slowing down, and Army National Guard Soldiers are playing a critical role in response efforts across the country," says Lt. Col. Sabrina Zowada, Chief of the National Guard Bureau's Marketing and Advertising Branch. "Disasterville is a one-of-a-kind perspective for students to see how and when the Guard is showing up in their communities, and experience the real skills and impact of these important missions." 

Disasterville is transforming high school gyms from September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga.

Students Work Together to Respond to Common Missions

Disasterville uses advanced mixed-reality technology to create three 10-minute missions most common to Army National Guard response efforts. Working together in teams of five, students are called to service at the following sites:

  • Wildfire: Amid a raging wildfire, teams work together to push back fires encroaching on a home in Disaster Canyon. Students will put out small wildfires, combine forces to push back larger flare-ups, save animals, and dodge falling trees. 
  • Flood Zone: After a major hurricane, civilians are fighting to stay above water on the streets they call home. Students will board their Zodiac and use headlamps to find and safely evacuate survivors while avoiding dangerous wildlife and other lurking hazards.
  • Earthquake: After a devastating earthquake, a train carrying hazardous chemicals and passengers derails, pinning civilians and spilling dangerous material, poisoning the air. Time ticks down as students arm themselves with the jaws of life to rescue survivors and clean up debris, all before the train gives way under its own weight.

"We saw firsthand how students connected with the Disasterville experience. They didn't just learn about disaster response—they felt the responsibility," says Lt. Col. Zawada. "Today's young people want purpose; they want action, and they want to know how they can contribute to something meaningful. We're excited to show even more students how the Guard meets that need."

Mixed-Reality Technology Brings Immersion and Impact

Disasterville utilizes advanced mixed-reality technology with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) graphics mapped to large plywood structures, creating a free-roam virtual neighborhood experience in high school gyms. Students wear virtual reality headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, and hazards, rescuing people in need. The technology also features advanced hand tracking, eliminating the need for game controllers and allowing students to interact with others and physically use in-game props and Army National Guard rescue tools like oars, hoses, chainsaws, and the jaws of life.  

Extended reality (XR) industry expert Dale Carman helped the Army bring the Disasterville experience to life. Carman is the co-founder and executive creative director at Groove Jones, which has over 25 years of experience in feature films, immersive tech, and branded productions.

A specialized tour crew will be present at each tour stop to guide participants safely through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about service.   

For more information on the Army National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

Supplementary Information

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is Disasterville, and how does the experience work?

A: Disasterville is a mixed-reality experience from the U.S. Army National Guard touring the nation, transforming gymnasiums into full-scale, mission-oriented disaster zones to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies through hands-on simulations. Students wear Meta Quest 3 headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, hazards, and people in need. Students are guided firsthand through high-tech, virtual missions, working together in teams to tackle three disaster zones -- wildfire, flood zone, and earthquake -- the same way as the Guard, by combining communication, physical endurance, and ingenuity to save lives, landscape, and their communities.

Q: Where will Disasterville be traveling?

A: Following a successful 2026 spring tour, Disasterville will head to even more high schools September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga. At each tour stop, a specialized tour crew will ensure the safety of and guide participants through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about Guard service.   

Q: What do Army National Guard Soldiers do? Where and how do they serve?

A: With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers serve part-time to support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Serving at least one weekend a month and two weeks a year, National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to pursue their civilian personal and professional passions.

Q: Where can I learn more about opportunities in the Army National Guard?

A: For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

About the Army National Guard (ARNG):

With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Army National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to serve part-time across medical, aviation, law enforcement, transportation, and engineering fields and beyond, while also pursuing their personal and professional goals through a civilian career or higher education. For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

WHEATON, Ill., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- T2 Capital Management, a fully integrated private equity real estate investment firm with $1.6 billion+ in AUM, today announced the launch of Base Living, the firm's wholly-owned, tech-enabled property management company. At launch, Base Living manages more than 850 multifamily units across three properties, as well as a 1 million-square foot-industrial property within T2's portfolio. Moving forward, Base Living will systematically expand operations across T2's entire portfolio including student housing, building on T2's proven track record and expertise in the sector.

With the launch of Base Living, T2 welcomes Tyler Yates as Director of Property Management, where he is responsible for operational and financial performance of T2's property portfolio, ensuring high standards of service and maximizing returns. Tyler manages Base Living's 24 new team members across Illinois, Indiana, and Florida, and is supported by eight members of T2's corporate team. He reports to Aaron Tink, Principal of T2, who oversees the firm's asset management division and leads Base Living. Tyler brings more than a decade of residential operating experience across student housing and multifamily. He most recently served as Vice President of Central Operations and Asset Management at Kairos Living, where he oversaw a national portfolio of 5,000+ homes, 125+ full-time employees, and more than 350 vendors.

"Tyler's deep industry experience and proven track record make him the right leader to drive this venture forward," said Aaron Tink. "Base Living brings institutional expertise, technology-enabled execution and hands-on decision-making to every aspect of property management, strengthening T2's fully integrated real estate platform from ownership through operations."

Base Living utilizes Entrata as its core property management platform, providing one integrated system for leasing, communications, payments, maintenance, accounting, renewals, and reporting in order to eliminate duplications and disconnected handoffs. The firm also utilizes best in class artificial intelligence platforms spanning the full resident journey from prospect engagement and tour scheduling to maintenance coordination and lease renewals.

"At T2, we have always believed that successful real estate ownership requires a deep understanding of the assets and communities we serve", said Jeff Brown, CEO and Co-Founder at T2 Capital Management. "Base Living serves as a direct bridge between our ownership strategy and daily, on the ground execution. By leveraging real time information and company wide accountability, Base Living enables us to optimize the resident experience while maximizing value creation across our portfolio."

Base Living is headquartered at 100 N. Main Street, Wheaton, Illinois, alongside T2's office.

ABOUT T2 CAPITAL MANAGEMENT

Headquartered in Wheaton, Illinois with a second location in Nashville, T2 was founded in 2011. As a fully integrated real estate investment firm, T2 provides multiple investment strategies that cover each aspect of the capital stack within commercial real estate. T2 actively pursues acquisition and development opportunities in the student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent space within select domestic growth markets. Through a separate business line, the firm also acts as a balance sheet lender having capitalized hundreds of projects totaling over $1.5 billion nationwide.
